title: Boss: a route engine
summary: Build the pieces of a tiny Camel in C#, then write a leak-free route for it.

steps.title: The brief
body: To really understand what a route does to an exchange, you will build a miniature route engine: header removal
with Camel's patterns, a step runner with the leaky HTTP producer from lesson 4, and then a route that is safe
in both directions despite that producer.

steps.title: removeHeaders with patterns
prompt: Camel's `removeHeaders` takes a `pattern` and an optional `excludePattern`. Each is either `*` (every header),
a prefix ending in `*` (`Camel*`), or an exact name. Names compare ignoring case.
The tests declare `Exchange` (case-insensitive `Headers`).
Write `bool Matches(string name, string? pattern)` (a null pattern matches nothing) and
`void RemoveHeaders(Exchange ex, string pattern, string? exclude)` that removes every header matching `pattern` but not `exclude`.
starter: void RemoveHeaders(Exchange ex, string pattern, string? exclude)
solution: void RemoveHeaders(Exchange ex, string pattern, string? exclude)
hints: Check `*` first, then `EndsWith("*")` for prefixes, then exact.
Iterate over `ex.Headers.Keys.ToList()`: you can't remove from a dictionary while enumerating it directly.
template: Dojo.Eq("prefix pattern does not match others", false, Matches("Cookie", "Camel*"));
Dojo.Eq("exact name, any case", true, Matches("ISBN", "isbn"));
Dojo.Eq("null pattern matches nothing", false, Matches("isbn", null));
Dojo.Eq("remove all except isbn", "isbn", string.Join(",", dojoA.Headers.Keys));
Dojo.Eq("remove Camel headers only", "Authorization,Cookie,isbn", string.Join(",", dojoB.Headers.Keys));
public Dictionary<string, string> Headers { get; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
public Dictionary<string, object?> Variables { get; } = new();

steps.title: The step runner
prompt: Steps are string arrays, mirroring the YAML:
| Step | Does |
| `["setVariable", name, simpleExpr]` | sets a variable to the evaluated expression |
| `["setHeader", name, simpleExpr]` | sets a header |
| `["setBody", simpleExpr]` | sets the body |
| `["removeHeaders", pattern]` or `["removeHeaders", pattern, exclude]` | as in the previous step |
| `["toD", uriExpr]` | calls `http(url, headersSent)` with the **simplified leaky producer**, see below |
For `toD`: `url` = the `CamelHttpUri` header if present, else the evaluated `uriExpr`; then append the `CamelHttpPath` header if present.

`headersSent` = every header not starting with `Camel` (case-insensitive dictionary). Afterwards: body = response body, every response header is copied onto the exchange, and `CamelHttpResponseCode` = the status as a string.

An unknown step name throws `ArgumentException`. `Simple`, `Matches` and `RemoveHeaders` are in your editor; write `void Run(List<string[]> steps, Exchange ex, Func<string, Dictionary<string, string>, (int Status, string Body, Dictionary<string, string> Headers)> http)`.

steps.title: Write the leak-free route
prompt: The engine from the previous step is now provided (as `Engine.Run`), complete with its **leaky** HTTP producer, plus a step
`["jqBook"]` that reshapes the body to `{"isbn":...,"title":...}`, and `["log", expr]`.
Write `List<string[]> GetBookRoute()` returning the steps for `GET /books/{isbn}` so that:
- the backend is called at exactly `http://catalogue:8080/api/books/{isbn}` and receives **only** `X-Trace-Id` = the exchange id;
- the body is reshaped with `jqBook`;
- the consumer's response has **only** the header `Content-Type: application/json` (none of the backend's headers, no `Camel*` headers);
- a log line `"[{exchangeId}] book {isbn}"` is written (anywhere in the route).
**Run checks** sends an exchange carrying the usual incoming headers (`isbn`, `CamelHttpUri`, `CamelHttpPath`, `CamelHttpMethod`, `Authorization`, `Cookie`).
hints: Copy the isbn into a variable before anything removes headers.
Remove every header before the call and again after it; then set the two headers you mean to send.
template: var dojoSeen = new List<(string Url, Dictionary<string, string> Headers)>();
Dojo.Eq("backend headers", "X-Trace-Id=ex-77", string.Join(";", dojoSeen[0].Headers.Select(kv => kv.Key + "=" + kv.Value)));
Dojo.Eq("response headers", "Content-Type=application/json", string.Join(";", dojoEx.Headers.Select(kv => kv.Key + "=" + kv.Value)));
Dojo.Check("log line written", Engine.Log.Contains("[ex-77] book 9780134757599"), "expected a log line \"[ex-77] book 9780134757599\"; got: " + string.Join(" | ", Engine.Log));

// The simplified HTTP producer from lesson 4: CamelHttpUri replaces the address, CamelHttpPath is appended,
// and every non-Camel header is sent. Response headers are merged back onto the exchange.
public static void Run(List<string[]> steps, Exchange ex, Func<string, Dictionary<string, string>, (int Status, string Body, Dictionary<string, string> Headers)> http)
if (Matches(name, s[1]) && !Matches(name, s.Length > 2 ? s[2] : null)) ex.Headers.Remove(name);
